scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You hit send on an email, and seconds later it lands in an inbox on the other side of the world. What's the route?

scenes.name: out
scenes.text: Your mail app hands the message to your provider's outgoing mail server, using a protocol called SMTP.

scenes.name: mx
scenes.text: That server looks at the part after the at sign, and asks the internet's address book, DNS, which server handles mail for that domain.

scenes.name: deliver
scenes.text: It connects to the recipient's mail server and passes the message across, usually encrypted along the way.

scenes.name: check
scenes.text: The receiving server checks it isn't spam or a fake sender, using records that prove where the email really came from.

scenes.name: store
scenes.text: The email is saved in the recipient's mailbox on that server. It waits there.

scenes.name: fetch
scenes.text: When they open their app, it syncs with the server and the email appears, on every device they use.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Send, look up, deliver, sync. Mail at internet speed. Follow for more on how things really work.
